author: agent:claude-code
message: Keep the answer to Claude Code's personal and work profiles on every archetype, configurable per host where it was asked

title: Asked by vg-dotfiles-windows: Claude Code's personal and work profiles on every archetype, configurable per host
body:
Claude Code's personal and work profiles on every archetype, configurable per host (graft:01a165bb-c28b..3f79, from vg-dotfiles-windows)

What was needed:
- vg-dotfiles-windows: vgmacbook already gives the user two Claude Code profiles (personal and work); make that one shared module every Nix archetype uses (nix-darwin, NixOS desktops, NixOS-WSL, the headless servers), with a per-host option saying which of the two it gets: both by default, or only one (e.g. a server that only does work), or none. The convention to match, as on Windows (vg-dotfiles-windows home/powershell/functions/claude.ps1): `claude` runs Claude Code with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-personal and `claude-work` with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work, each clearing CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN so one profile's token never leaks into the other, and each calling the real binary rather than itself. Keeping the two config dirs separate is the point: their logins, settings, sessions and memory stay apart, so the same names and dirs on every machine mean a session started on one host can be found on another with the same profile. If the darwin version already differs from this, say which way is right and both sides can follow.

Answer (done): Done in vg-dotfiles 4462eaf (not pushed yet), following Windows' convention: every Nix host gets `claude` (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-personal) and `claude-work` (~/.claude-work), each clearing CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and exec'ing the real binary; a host opts into one or none with common.claude-code.profiles. The macOS and WSL version differed (dirs under ~/.local/share/claude-profiles, token not cleared); it now matches Windows, and activation moves an old dir across. One difference kept: bare `claude` still follows a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR a project's direnv sets, which Windows has no counterpart for (`claude-work` always pins work). There's also a `claude-personal` alongside `claude`.
